pge:cc-e-rsmart-2025-10-31: Two provisions of the published Schedule E-RSMART are not represented in this filing at all, and a third is carried only as prose. The Sheet 5 Bill Protection transitional incentive, under which a new participant pays no more than it would have under its otherwise applicable schedule through its first full Summer Season, which for this purpose runs May 1 through October 31 rather than the June 1 through September 30 summer of the underlying residential schedules, computed cumulatively at the end of the season and credited on the next regular bill. The Sheet 2 bill-period multiplier on both credits: the SmartRate Non-High-Price Period Credit of $0.00636 per kWh and the Participation Credit of $0.00167 per kWh are each multiplied by the number of SmartDays falling in the bill period, and neither applies at all in a bill period containing no SmartDay. This filing carries the two per-event rates as its unit prices, and states the multiplier and the at-least-one-SmartDay condition only as prose on each credit's applicability rule, whose own machine-readable condition is an opaque yes-or-no predicate the consumer must evaluate; the SmartDay count itself appears nowhere as data. The Sheet 5 grandfathering for customers dual enrolled in SmartRate and SmartAC before October 26, 2018, who may remain in both programs but receive no demand response energy payment during the SmartDay High-Price Period. Two further items are scope decisions rather than gaps. The Sheet 4 activation trigger (an average day-ahead maximum temperature forecast for San Jose, Concord, Red Bluff, Sacramento and Fresno of 98 degrees Fahrenheit on non-holiday weekdays and 105 degrees on holidays and weekends, with CAISO alerts, high forecast spot prices and testing as further grounds, and PG&E retaining sole discretion not to call an event) settles which days are SmartDays rather than what a SmartDay costs, and is carried as prose on the price update rule together with the 4:00 to 9:00 p.m. High-Price Period, which is the same window on all five base schedules even though their own peak periods differ. The Sheet 1 enrollment gates (the SmartMeter requirement, the five-business-day lag before the next billing cycle, and the exclusions for master-metered, net energy metering, standby, direct access, community choice aggregation and Rule 22.1 transitional bundled service customers) are enrollment operations, so the filing carries a single eligibility condition: that the customer has elected SmartRate.
pge:cc-e-tou-c-2026-03-01: Five parts of the published Schedule E-TOU-C are not represented in this filing. The Special Condition 8 bill protection, which for twelve months after enrollment credits the customer the difference between what it paid on this schedule and what it would have paid on the tiered non-time-of-use Schedule E-1, with its own exclusions (customers on Schedules NEM2, NEM2V or NEM2VMSH who start or transfer service on or after October 1, 2020, customers opting in from another time-of-use plan, and customers requesting enrollment after May 4, 2022) and a parallel twelve-month version on Sheet 9 covering the non-generation charges of community choice aggregation and direct access customers. The Wildfire Fund Charge exemption: Sheet 1 states that customers receiving a medical baseline allowance do not pay this charge and Special Condition 11 excludes CARE and medical baseline sales from it, but the filing carries the $0.00591 per kWh charge with no applicability condition, so it is priced for every customer. The Sheet 4 unbundling of the base services charge into its Distribution, Public Purpose Program, Nuclear Decommissioning and New System Generation components for each income tier; only the three daily totals ($0.19713, $0.39688 and $0.79343) are modeled. The second qualification path for Income Tier 2, an affordable rental unit in a property listed in the California Housing Partnership's database and restricted to residents at or below 80 percent of Area Median Income; only the FERA path is modeled, so a customer qualifying through affordable housing alone resolves to the Tier 3 charge. And the Sheet 1 instruction that time-of-use period usage be assigned to baseline tiers pro rata, so that a customer with twenty percent of its usage in the peak period has twenty percent of the usage in each tier treated as on-peak: this filing carries the time-of-use dimension and the sibling baseline-tier modifier carries the tier dimension, but nothing states how the two combine. Three things are out of scope rather than missing. The standby reservation charges the Applicability section imports from Schedule S Special Conditions 1 through 6 for customers partly supplied from a nonutility source are charges of another schedule, and with them go the Special Condition 9 and 10 exemptions for sub-megawatt non-exporting solar and for distributed energy resources. Special Condition 6's designation of a primary meter and additional meters, and Special Condition 7's one-time option for a separately metered common-area account to move to a general service schedule, are customer-service procedures and not rates.
pge:cc-e-tou-c-vintage-pcia-2026-03-01: This modifier carries the eighteen vintage Power Charge Indifference Adjustment rates published on Sheet 8, from $0.02973 per kWh for the 2009 vintage to a credit of $0.01011 per kWh for the 2025 and 2026 vintages, gated on a residential customer taking generation service through community choice aggregation, direct access or transitional bundled service. What it does not carry is the other half of the same instruction. Sheet 8 states that these customers pay every charge in the Unbundling of Total Rates except the Bundled Power Charge Indifference Adjustment and the generation charge, but the base filing's bundled adjustment (a credit of $0.01011 per kWh) and its four seasonal generation energy prices carry no condition excluding them, and this modifier records the replacement only in its description prose, so a consumer applying the base plan together with this modifier will charge a departed customer both the bundled and the vintaged adjustment as well as PG&E generation. Three further charges Sheet 8 directs the same customers to are absent because they live in other schedules: the franchise fee surcharge under Schedule E-FFS for community choice aggregation and direct access customers, the short-term commodity prices under Schedule TBCC for transitional bundled service customers, and the exemptions set out in Schedules DA CRS and CCA CRS, including those for medical baseline customers and for continuous direct access service.
pge:cc-e-tou-c-baseline-tier-2026-03-01: This modifier carries the Special Condition 1 baseline quantities for all ten baseline territories in both Code B (basic) and Code H (all-electric) form across both seasons, with the Baseline Credit of $0.08140 per kWh on within-baseline usage and the Conservation Incentive Adjustment at a $0.02786 credit within baseline and a $0.05354 charge above it. Three provisions bearing on those quantities are not represented. Special Condition 5's standard medical quantities, Code M (basic plus medical) and Code S (all-electric plus medical), which are added to the Special Condition 1 quantity to raise the ceiling on usage billed at baseline rates, with further quantities available under Rule 19 for both the primary and additional meters. URPX v0.5.1 states a service bracket's bounds as absolute numbers and offers no way to carry an allowance that shifts an existing bound, so representing Code M and Code S means recomputing every one of the forty territory, code and season cells rather than stating the addition once; they are therefore absent rather than approximated. Special Condition 4's seasonal proration, under which a bill spanning the June 1 or October 1 changeover multiplies each season's daily baseline quantity by the number of days of that season in the billing period: the published quantities are kWh per day, and the brackets here carry those figures as plain kWh bounds with no daily basis, so a consumer must scale them to the billing period itself. Special Conditions 3 and 6 on dwellings served by more than one meter, under which the all-electric quantities are allocated only to the meter the customer designates as primary and an additional meter receives only the basic, or basic plus medical, quantity; the matrix here prices a single meter.
pge:cc-nbt-2025-10-17: This filing carries the full Export Compensation Rate surface, 4,608 prices covering twelve months by twenty-four hours by weekday and weekend for each of the 2023 through 2026 interconnection vintages, split into the Generation and Delivery components that Sheet 11 step 6 sums into the customer-facing rate. Three things the published schedule states are not represented. The Sheet 11 ACC Plus adder is carried for the 2025 vintage only, at $0.01320 per kWh residential and $0.05400 per kWh low income; the 2023, 2024, 2026 and 2027 rows of the same table ($0.02200 and $0.09000, $0.01760 and $0.07200, $0.00880 and $0.03600, $0.00440 and $0.01800) are not, and neither are the four exclusions Sheet 11 attaches to the adder, for customers transitioning from legacy NEM or NEM2 at the end of their legacy period, customers who bought a building with an existing system, non-residential customers, and customers required to install solar by building code. Special Condition 5 Net Surplus Compensation, paid at true-up on generation exceeding consumption over the customer's Relevant Period at a rolling twelve-month average of PG&E's default load aggregation point price between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m., together with its renewable attribute adder and the Special Condition 2.h energy true-up, which carries unused generation and delivery credits into the next Relevant Period, together with the Special Condition 2.e rule that those credits are forfeited at the last true-up once the customer is no longer served under the tariff; these settle over a year rather than a billing period, and the filing prices only the per-hour export credit. The Special Condition 2.d through 2.f rules on what an export credit may offset: generation export credits reduce only volumetric generation charges and delivery export credits only volumetric delivery charges, and four non-bypassable charges (Public Purpose Program, Nuclear Decommissioning Charge, Competition Transition Charge and Wildfire Fund Charge) may not be reduced by export credits at all, though ACC Plus credits may offset any charge. Scope is the residential NBT-S sub-schedule taking Schedule E-ELEC as its otherwise applicable schedule, so the Sheet 13 sub-schedules NBT-EXP, NBT-EXP-OTR, NBT-MT, NBT-PS and NBTA are absent, as are Special Condition 4 multiple tariff facilities, Special Condition 6 load aggregation, Special Condition 8 paired storage, Special Condition 9 disaster provisions and Special Condition 10 prevailing wage, which conditions a project's eligibility to interconnect rather than what its exports are worth.
